patterns.reminder: This looks like a Resend API key. Sending keys are set by each person on their own screen and kept in R2 (settings/person/...); none belongs in the code, a test or a log. Remove it, and report the key as exposed rather than rewriting history.

This looks like an Anthropic API key. The spam check's key is set on the mailbox's settings screen and kept in R2; none belongs in the code, a test or a log. Remove it, and report the key as exposed rather than rewriting history.

This looks like a Cloudflare Turnstile secret key. Root sets it on /root and it is kept in R2 (settings/turnstile.json); none belongs in the code, a test or a log. Remove it, and report the key as exposed.

This looks like a Cloudflare API token written out. It lives only in the repository's Actions secrets and reaches only the workflow steps that run wrangler (workflowGuards.test.ts); never in a file. Remove it, and report the token as exposed.

This looks like a private key (PEM, or the private part of a JWK such as a VAPID key). A key the running Worker needs is a Worker secret (wrangler secret put), never a value in the code. The only allowed one is the test-only VAPID key in tests/vitest.config.mts.

A key-like name is being given a value in a Wrangler config file. Everything under `vars` is committed in plain text and shown in the deploy log. A key the Worker needs is a Worker secret (wrangler secret put), and only its name may appear here, in a comment.
